item.title: Hinai-jidori: One of Japan's Three Great Chickens — Akita Guide
item.description: Hinai-jidori is one of Japan’s three designated premium chicken breeds, raised free-range in Akita’s Hinai region for around 150 days — twice as long as standard poultry. The meat is firmer, richer and far more intensely flavoured than supermarket chicken. Taste it in kiritanpo hot pot, grilled yakitori, an oyakodon rice bowl, or even as chicken sashimi at specialist restaurants. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Odate/Hinai & Akita City Hours Restaurant hours Admission Varies by dish Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round What to Try Firm, rich Hinai-jidori in kiritanpo hot pot.

item.title: Iburigakko: Akita's Smoked Daikon Pickles — Guide
item.description: Iburigakko is a beloved Akita farmhouse specialty — daikon radish smoke-dried over wood fires, then pickled in rice bran, producing a crunchy, deeply smoky, gently sweet pickle. Traditionally made in snowbound winter farmhouses where radishes couldn’t sun-dry, it pairs superbly with sake and, in a modern twist, with cream cheese. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Inland Akita (Yokote etc.) Hours Shop hours Admission Cheap (packs) Time needed About 20 min Best time Year-round; made in winter What to Try Crunchy, smoky pickled daikon slices.

item.title: Kiritanpo Nabe: Akita's Iconic Rice Hot Pot — Guide
item.description: Kiritanpo is Akita’s most iconic dish — freshly pounded rice is moulded onto cedar skewers, grilled over charcoal, then simmered in a rich broth with Hinai-jidori chicken (one of Japan’s three great chickens), burdock, Japanese parsley and maitake mushrooms. The mochi-like kiritanpo soaks up the umami broth beautifully. Best from October to March. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Akita City & Odate, Akita Hours Restaurant hours Admission ~¥1,200–2,000 a set Time needed About 1 hour Best time Oct–Mar (winter) What to Try Grilled kiritanpo rice skewers in a rich hot pot.

item.title: Best Hotels & Ryokan in Akita: Nyuto Onsen, Kakunodate & More
item.description: Akita Prefecture is one of Japan’s most rewarding destinations for travellers who want authentic, uncrowded ryokan experiences. Nyuto Onsenkyo — a cluster of seven isolated hot spring inns deep in the Towada-Hachimantai National Park mountains — is often cited by Japanese travellers as the most atmospheric onsen destination in the entire country. Best Areas to Stay Nyuto Onsenkyo — Japan’s Most Atmospheric Onsen Seven separate hot spring inns tucked in a forested mountain valley near Lake Tazawa.
